Hi Liam — thanks for the quick report and the traces. We’re looking into this as a priority. Short answers / immediate mitigations you can try now: 

1) Temporarily disable streaming and use short-polling (non-streaming generation) for high-sensitivity flows — this avoids partial-token backpressure and will reduce perceived pauses.
2) Reduce the request history you send (prune older turns) to keep input context under ~1,500 tokens for now.
3) In the SDK, reduce `stream_chunk_ms` to 150ms and set `max_concurrent_requests` to 6.
4) If you have access to a Dedicated region, route heavy sessions to eu-west-1 Dedicated pool (we can open capacity if needed).

Kimberly / team — initial triage from infra and runtime: we’re seeing a pattern on eu-edge shards where KV cache churn spikes when sessions include long histories combined with a recent memory-path kernel selection change (deployed 2027-04-20 02:10 UTC). The kernel change causes slower host->device memcpy for certain small-buffer streaming codepaths on the A100 fleet we use in eu-edge; that, coupled with frequent KV cache evictions, yields intermittent stalls as the runtime waits for KV refill + memcpy.

Immediate mitigations we can coordinate (ordered by risk/impact):
A) Roll back the kernel selector for eu-edge streaming codepath — this is the fastest infra-side mitigation and will be done if customer impact increases beyond 10% of sessions. Ops runbook excerpt attached.
B) Toggle session-level prefix caching TTL to 30m for affected sessions (server-side config). This will reduce KV churn; we can flip it for Acme via a temporary routing rule.
C) For customers using the streaming SDK, reduce `stream_chunk_tokens` on the server to 8 tokens per chunk to reduce the memcpy frequency pressure.
D) Route heavy sessions to Dedicated eu-west-1 where the affected kernel variant is not in use — we can provision a temporary capacity burst for Acme.
E) Apply a server-side per-session soft-rate limit (e.g., 2 reqs/sec) to protect shard memory under load; this will slightly increase latency for very aggressive clients but will prevent stalls.

We’ve opened OPS ticket OPS-9876 and a support ticket ACME-5421. I’ll coordinate rollback in the next 60–180 minutes if telemetry shows the situation worsening.
